Tax, interest or penalty liability - Deceased person - Recovery from heir - Attachment of bank account - Deceased father ran proprietorship business, namely, M/s. Oriental Facility with separate GSTIN that was cancelled before demise - Petitioner son ran independent proprietorship in labour supply under same trade name but with separate GSTIN and from different premises - Department issued DRC-07 raising demand against deceased father’s proprietorship and DRC-13 was issued to petitioner’s banker to recover such dues - Petitioner’s personal bank account was frozen without prior notice or hearing - No SCN or adjudication had determined petitioner’s liability as legal representative or as person continuing business - HELD : Similarity of trade name alone could not establish succession or continuation - Separate GSTINs and places of business signified distinct taxable persons - Absence of prior determination rendered recovery impermissible - Recovery powers presupposed established liability and required prior adjudication upon notice based on tangible material - A bank account constitutes property within meaning of Article 300A of Constitution of India and hence, freezing Petitioner's bank account without any SCN and/or opportunity to put forth objections results in violation of his constitutional rights since he has been deprived of his property, without due process of law being followed - Petitioner's bank account was to be de-frozen - However, liberty was to be given to proceed in law following due process [Section  93,  read with sections  79  and  83, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Article 300A, read with article 226, of Constitution of India] [Paras 20 and 21] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Current account and Cash credit account - Communication in Form DRC-22 was addressed by Principal Commissioner to Bank Manager directing that proceedings had been lodged against petitioner under section 83 of CGST Act and, therefore, current account of petitioner was to be provisionally attached - Petitioner submitted that by virtue of attachment of account, apart from debit transfers all accounts were debit freezed - Not only current account, but in fact cash credit account was also provisionally attached - On writ, HELD : On more than one occasion, Court had deprecated practice of respondent authorities in seeking to enforce tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account - Notice was issued to respondent/s - Till returnable date, there would be ad-interim relief [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5, 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]GST : Revenue authority's practice of enforcing tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account, should be deprecated

Provisional Attachment -  Bank Account - During search of assessee's business premises, revenue found two Backhoe Loaders (JCB) - Impugned order was passed attaching assessee's bank account under section 83 - Assessee contended that no tax amount had been determined or demanded from assessee and Commissioner had no material to form opinion that attachment of bank account was necessary to protect interest of Government Revenue - HELD : Power to cause attachment of a bank account is drastic in nature, inasmuch as, it could in certain situations, bring business of a taxable person to a grinding halt - Before attachment is levied, Commissioner has to form an opinion that for purpose of protecting interest of Government Revenue, it is necessary to attach any property, including bank account of taxable person - This opinion has to be based on material, and cannot be on basis of assumptions and presumptions of Commissioner - In instant case, proceedings under Section 67 stood concluded and there was no determination of any tax amount, or even calling upon Petitioner to show-cause as to why any tax amount ought not to be recovered from him - No proceedings for raising a demand on Petitioner had been filed till date - This apart, before attachment is levied, Commissioner has to form an opinion that for purpose of protecting interest of Government Revenue, it is necessary to attach any property, including Bank Account of taxable person - This opinion has to be based on material, and cannot be on basis of assumptions and presumptions of Commissioner - Impugned order did not set out any material which formed basis of opinion for attaching bank account of assessee - No material which led Commissioner to believe that attachment was necessary to secure interest of Revenue was communicated to assessee - Impugned order was to be set aside [Section  83, read with section  67, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6 to 8] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank accounts - Some bank accounts having "0" credit balance - Provisional attachment of bank accounts was to be lifted provided cumulative amount appearing as credit balance in all bank accounts remitted to respondent/revenue, to protect its interests, pending adjudication [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8 and 11] [In favour of assessee]GST : Provisional attachment of bank accounts should be lifted provided that cumulative amount appearing as credit balance in all bank accounts was remitted to revenue to protect its interests, pending adjudication

Provisional attachment- Renewal/Revival of attachment - Assessee was subjected to provisional attachment under section 83 for 4th time - Assessee challenged same vide instant petition relying on judgement of supreme court in Kesari Nandan Mobile v. Asstt. CST [2025] 177 taxmann.com 481 (SC) - HELD: Supreme Court in Kesari Nandan (supra) clearly held that when statute does not provide for an extension, renewal, reissuance, revival, same cannot be done by authorities and such an action would amount executive overreaching statute - In light of same, impugned order attaching bank account of assessee was to be quashed and set aside - Authorities were to be directed to immediately de-freeze bank account of assessee [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8 and 9] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment of bank accounts - Principal Additional Director General merely stated that powers conferred on concerned official under section 83 was invoked for provisionally attaching bank accounts of petitioner in order to protect interest of revenue - However, order did not show any basis for formation of opinion that provisional attachment was necessary to safeguard revenue's interest - No tangible material was disclosed - Order breached mandatory pre-conditions for exercise of powers under section 83 ibid [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 9, 10 and12] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - De-freezing denied - Petitioner, GST-registered technology service provider in Gujarat, acted as TSP for Digihub, facilitating payouts through current account with virtual accounts at respondent bank - GST authorities, probing Digihub tax evasion, provisionally attached petitioner accounts under Section 83 - Second attachment order followed - Petitioner sought quashing and de-freezing - Department cited payouts from petitioner accounts to beneficiaries of online gaming/betting funds, discrepancies, 35,064 linked accounts under examination, and petitioner admission of not verifying Digihub credentials - HELD : Facts were undisputed - Record showed Digihub used petitioner platform and bank account for gaming or betting payouts - Petitioner non-verification stood admitted and reliance on undertaking from Digihub was insufficient - No effort was made to check website or invoices to ascertain business nature - Considering enormity of transactions and ongoing investigation, attachment was justified and de-freezing was declined - Writ petition was dismissed [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 7 and 8] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Petitioner challenged provisional attachment of its bank accounts under Section 83 - DRC-22 recorded that Section 74 proceedings had been launched and froze PAN-linked accounts - A writ was filed before High Court - HELD: Section 83 applies only to protect revenue on a reasoned opinion based on tangible material - This draconian power requires cogent reasons - letters contain only a bald assertion of Section 74 proceedings, with no specific grounds - In fact, no proceedings under Section 74 were initiated - attachments are perverse, arbitrary and without basis in law - Provisional attachment notices dated 23 July 2025 are quashed and release directed within 48 hours, liberty to proceed afresh [Section  83,  read with section  74,  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7 to 11] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank accounts - Some bank accounts having "0" credit balance - Provisional attachment of bank accounts was to be lifted provided cumulative amount appearing as credit balance in all bank accounts remitted to respondent/revenue, to protect its interests, pending adjudication [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 8 and 11] [In favour of assessee]

II Section 83 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery -  Provisional attachment - Whether on facts under heading 'Demands and recovery - Determination of tax' since nothing was demonstrated by department either in orders of attachment or in affidavit filed as to why exercise of such drastic power of attachment of bank accounts was necessary, provisional attachment of assessee's bank accounts was to be removed - Held, yes [Paras 16  17] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - De-attachment - Petitioner became aware that its bank account was directed to be frozen by an communication issued by Bank - Although files produced by revenue indicated that there were allegations of wrongful availment of Input Tax Credit by assessee and respondent authorities were also investigating chain of suppliers, there was no order passed by Commissioner recording his satisfaction that orders of provisional attachment were necessary to safeguard interests of revenue - Revenue's case was that no order under section 83 of CGST Act was operating against petitioner and communications issued to various suppliers had been withdrawn - HELD : So far as provisional attachment of bank account is concerned, same would have lapsed by virtue of section 83(2) of CGST Act - Communications issued to assessee's customers restraining them from making any payment against supplies made by assessee was also without authority of law - Thus, assessee's grievance did not survive [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 12] [In favour of assessee/Writ disposed]GST : Although files produced by revenue indicated that there were allegations of wrongful availment of Input Tax Credit by assessee and respondent authorities were also investigating chain of suppliers, there was no order passed by Commissioner recording his satisfaction that orders of provisional attachment were necessary to safeguard interests of revenue; provisional attachment being no longer operative, writ petition was disposed

Provisional attachment  - Illegal account attachment - Petitioner maintained current account with HDFC Bank - Officer-in-Charge, Itanagar Police Station instructed bank to freeze account - Bank complied - Assistant Commissioner, CGST later indicated that during probe into M/s Siddhi Vinayak Trade Merchants, input tax credit of about Rs. 1.84 lakhs had been passed to account of petitioner - Petitioner immediately replied to said communication stating that petitioner was in no way connected with Siddhi Vinayak Trade Merchants and he had no transaction with said firm - After sending said reply, petitioner also reverted amount of Rs. 1.84 lakh back in the account of Siddhi Vinayak Trade Merchants - Petitioner submitted that Police station without any authority directed bank to freeze account, due to which petitioner was facing difficulty running its business - Police authorities and bank were impleaded - Despite service, respondent police did not appear - No authorizing order was produced - No further communication from police reached bank after initial instruction - No step for judicial approval was taken - HELD: Freezing rested solely on police instruction without judicial authorization - It was noted that no order by competent Magistrate under relevant CrPC provisions was placed by any respondent - Police direction to freeze account was bad in law - Bank was directed to defreeze petitioner’s account and permit operations [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Section  106,  read with section  107,  of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023] [Paras 10 and 11] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Contempt proceedings - Bank account of assessee was attached on ground that assessee had wrongly availed input tax credit in contravention of section 16(2) on strength of invoices issued by fake/bogus GSTIN entities - Direction was issued to defreeze bank account of assessee - Assessee filed instant contempt petition against respondent authority - Respondent authority made statement that letter for de-freezing of bank accounts of assessee had been issued - HELD : In view of statement made by respondent authority that letter for de-freezing of bank accounts had been issued, instant contempt case was to be closed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Jharkhand Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 2] [In favour of revenue]GST : Where pursuant to High Court's order, letter for de-freezing of bank accounts of assessee had been issued, contempt case filed by assessee against authority alleging non-compliance was to be closed

Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Assessee challenged order freezing its bank account under Section 83 of CGST Act, 2017 - Revenue tax authorities justified attachment based on assessee’s failure to respond to notices and non-cooperation in tax proceedings - HELD: Power under Section 83 to provisionally attach property is draconian and can only be exercised upon formation of opinion based on tangible material that attachment is necessary to protect government revenue - Mere non-cooperation or failure to respond to notices does not justify provisional attachment - Tax authorities failed to produce cogent material showing reasonable apprehension of default - Impugned order quashed - Writ petition allowed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 12-17] [In favour of assessee]

Appellate Authority - Appeals to - Assessee had filed GST returns, however supplier of assessee had failed to make payment of GST - Revenue had proceeded against assessee and passed order and also freezed bank account of assessee - Assessee had filed appeal before Appellate Authority, whereby, they had paid sum of Rs. 83,000/- for accepting appeal, which was yet to be numbered by reveue - HELD : As per provision of Section 107 if assessee had paid 10% of outstanding tax dues along with penalty, revenue proceedings would be automatically stayed - In instant case, since assessee had paid a sum of Rs. 83,000/-, revenue was supposed to have de-freeze bank account of assessee as per Section 107 [Section 107 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]GST : Since assessee had deposited 10% of total outstanding tax dues along with penalty, bank account of assessee should be de-freezed as per section 107

Provisional attachment - Bank account - De-attachment - Petitioner became aware that its bank account was directed to be frozen by an communication issued by Bank - Although files produced by revenue indicated that there were allegations of wrongful availment of Input Tax Credit by assessee and respondent authorities were also investigating chain of suppliers, there was no order passed by Commissioner recording his satisfaction that orders of provisional attachment were necessary to safeguard interests of revenue - Revenue's case was that no order under section 83 of CGST Act was operating against petitioner and communications issued to various suppliers had been withdrawn - HELD : So far as provisional attachment of bank account is concerned, same would have lapsed by virtue of section 83(2) of CGST Act - Communications issued to assessee's customers restraining them from making any payment against supplies made by assessee was also without authority of law - Thus, assessee's grievance did not survive [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 12] [In favour of assessee/Writ disposed]

Provisional Attachment - Debit freezing of bank account - A notice had been issued to Branch Manager, ICICI Bank by officer in charge, PS Papumpare, Arunachal Pradesh to debit freeze bank account of petitioner - Accordingly, bank proceeded to debit freeze account of petition - Petitioner approached instant court by way instant writ petition before Calcutta High Court - CGST authorities submitted that account had been directed to be frozen in course of an investigation undertaken by police upon a complaint being lodged by CGST authorities in Arunachal Pradesh - Respondents further submitted that instant court lacked jurisdiction to entertain instant petition - Petitioner however submitted that instant petition was confined to arbitrary freezing of petitioner's account and entire cause of action had arisen within territorial jurisdiction of instant court as petitioner's account was within jurisdiction of instant court - HELD: Main part of cause of action had arisen within jurisdiction of instant Court - Since writ petition did not seek quashment either of proceedings initiated by CGST authorities or investigation conducted by police authorities and since it is only confined to order of debit freezing of her Bank account, therefore, writ petitioner would not be necessarily required to plead and prove illegality of investigation conducted by respondent police authorities or proceedings initiated by CGST authorities for purpose of instant writ petition - Petitioner clearly made out a case of her right being infringed by debit freezing of petitioner's bank account within territorial limit of instant Court's jurisdiction - There was nothing on record to show that Investigation Officer approached Magistrate and any seizure or attachment order had been passed or debit freezing had been reported to jurisdictional magistrate - Therefore, impugned notice could not be said to be in accordance with law and same was to be set aside - Bank was to be directed to allow petitioner to operate petitioner's account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Sections 106 and 107 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023]GST: Where petitioner’s bank account was frozen by order of police without following mandatory procedures of seizure reporting to Magistrate under Section 106 or obtaining Magistrate order under Section 107, such debit freezing was invalid and same was to be quashed, as police lacked authority to order such freeze without requisite Magistrate authorization

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Contempt proceedings - Bank account of assessee was attached on ground that assessee had wrongly availed input tax credit in contravention of section 16(2) on strength of invoices issued by fake/bogus GSTIN entities - Direction was issued to defreeze bank account of assessee - Assessee filed instant contempt petition against respondent authority - Respondent authority made statement that letter for de-freezing of bank accounts of assessee had been issued - HELD : In view of statement made by respondent authority that letter for de-freezing of bank accounts had been issued, instant contempt case was to be closed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Jharkhand Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 2] [In favour of revenue]

Provisional attachment of bank accounts - Principal Additional Director General merely stated that powers conferred on concerned official under section 83 was invoked for provisionally attaching bank accounts of petitioner in order to protect interest of revenue - However, order did not show any basis for formation of opinion that provisional attachment was necessary to safeguard revenue's interest - No tangible material was disclosed - Order breached mandatory pre-conditions for exercise of powers under section 83 ibid [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 9, 10 and12] [In favour of assessee]GST : Order of provisional attachment of bank accounts of assessee was not sustainable as it was passed without disclosing any specific reason based on tangible material available with revenue

Provisional Attachment - Debit freezing of bank account - A notice had been issued to Branch Manager, ICICI Bank by officer in charge, PS Papumpare, Arunachal Pradesh to debit freeze bank account of petitioner - Accordingly, bank proceeded to debit freeze account of petition - Petitioner approached instant court by way instant writ petition before Calcutta High Court - CGST authorities submitted that account had been directed to be frozen in course of an investigation undertaken by police upon a complaint being lodged by CGST authorities in Arunachal Pradesh - Respondents further submitted that instant court lacked jurisdiction to entertain instant petition - Petitioner however submitted that instant petition was confined to arbitrary freezing of petitioner's account and entire cause of action had arisen within territorial jurisdiction of instant court as petitioner's account was within jurisdiction of instant court - HELD: Main part of cause of action had arisen within jurisdiction of instant Court - Since writ petition did not seek quashment either of proceedings initiated by CGST authorities or investigation conducted by police authorities and since it is only confined to order of debit freezing of her Bank account, therefore, writ petitioner would not be necessarily required to plead and prove illegality of investigation conducted by respondent police authorities or proceedings initiated by CGST authorities for purpose of instant writ petition - Petitioner clearly made out a case of her right being infringed by debit freezing of petitioner's bank account within territorial limit of instant Court's jurisdiction - There was nothing on record to show that Investigation Officer approached Magistrate and any seizure or attachment order had been passed or debit freezing had been reported to jurisdictional magistrate - Therefore, impugned notice could not be said to be in accordance with law and same was to be set aside - Bank was to be directed to allow petitioner to operate petitioner's account [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Sections 106 and 107 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023]

Appellate Authority - Appeals to - Assessee had filed GST returns, however supplier of assessee had failed to make payment of GST - Revenue had proceeded against assessee and passed order and also freezed bank account of assessee - Assessee had filed appeal before Appellate Authority, whereby, they had paid sum of Rs. 83,000/- for accepting appeal, which was yet to be numbered by reveue - HELD : As per provision of Section 107 if assessee had paid 10% of outstanding tax dues along with penalty, revenue proceedings would be automatically stayed - In instant case, since assessee had paid a sum of Rs. 83,000/-, revenue was supposed to have de-freeze bank account of assessee as per Section 107 [Section 107 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional Attachment - Attachment of bank account - Show Cause Notice was issued against petitioner-assessee by respondent-department under Section 83 - Respondent issued attachment orders on ground that petitioner had failed to discharge tax liability without any justification, further, respondent was of opinion that there was every chance that petitioner might default in paying ultimate tax, interest and penalty, for which a demand might be raised in assessment proceedings on completion - Petitioner filed instant writ petition seeking setting aside of bank account attachment order issued by respondent - Held:Supreme Court had opined that power to order a provisional attachment [under Section 83] of property of taxable person, including a bank account, was draconian in nature and conditions which were prescribed by statute for a valid exercise of power must be strictly followed - Further, apex court had further opined that exercise of power for ordering a provisional attachment must be preceded by formation of an opinion by Commissioner that “it is necessary so to do” for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue - Expression “necessary so to do for protecting government revenue” implicates that interests of government revenue could not be protected without ordering a provisional attachment - As aforesaid order applies with full force to facts of present case, therefore, attachments in FORM GST DRC-22 dated 05.04.2024 and order passed under Section 83 also dated 05.04.2024 were to be quashed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 3-6] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where petitioner-assessee challenged provisional attachment of bank account under Section 83 and apex court held that provisional attachment of bank account could only take place if it was necessary so to do for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue, therefore, following aforesaid judgement, provisional attachment order was to be set aside

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - limitation period - Petitioner ran footwear shop at Paramakudi - Business stood in spouse name - Petitioner maintained savings bank account with third respondent bank - First respondent issued provisional attachment under Section 83 attaching bank account, pursuant to which bank froze account - Petitioner challenged attachment contending that under Section 83(2) such attachment ceased after one year - Respondent did not dispute factual matrix - HELD : Statutory limitation in Section 83(2) mandated cessation of provisional attachment after one year - Continued freezing beyond prescribed period was impermissible - Impugned attachment was set aside and petitioner was permitted to operate account [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 to 12] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment  -  Bank account- Lifting of attachment - Natural justice - Petitioner, a software company with operations in USA and India, was linked to DGGI Meerut probe concerning Redmil Business Mall India Pvt. Ltd. and Betterbot Tech Services Pvt. Ltd. - Summons dated 1 September 2025 and 8 September 2025 were issued to Director Finance for evidence and records - On 8 September 2025 ADG DGGI Meerut issued provisional attachment freezing eleven ICICI accounts, identifying one account and directing debit freeze on any account operated on same PAN - On 13 September 2025 petitioner sought withdrawal and personal hearing and hearing occurred on 23 September 2025 - By letter dated 25 September 2025 signed by Deputy Director DGGI objections were rejected and petitioner stated communication reached on 4 November 2025 - Preliminary probe alleged fraudulent ITC of about Rs 3.1 crores and petitioner deposited about Rs 40 lakhs - HELD : Petitioner was only a witness and no probe had commenced against petitioner - Freezing order preceded any response to summons and rejection letter was unreasoned, reflecting non-application of mind - Non-communication till 4 November 2025 violated natural justice and impeded remedies - Attachment of eleven accounts for alleged ITC of Rs 3.1 crores was prima facie disproportionate with debilitating business impact - Provisional attachment could not be continued at this stage and petitioner could operate accounts subject to maintaining Rs 1 crore in any attached account [Section  83,  read with section  169  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule  159  of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 15 to 17 and 22] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Validity of - Competent Authority by an order passed under section 83 provisionally attached bank account of assessee - Assessee contended before High Court that no proceedings were pending against it under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 and hence jurisdictional fact for issuance of order of provisional attachment being non-existent, impugned order was ultra vires section 83 - HELD : Revenue had not disputed that no proceedings under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 had yet been initiated against assessee - Impugned order of provisional attachment required to be set aside with direction to Competent Authority to defreeze bank account of assessee immediately [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 4 and 5] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where Competent Authority provisionally attached bank account of assessee but no proceedings under section 62 or 63 or 64 or 67 or 73 or 74 had yet been initiated, impugned order required to be set aside

Provisional Attachment - Attachment of bank account - Show Cause Notice was issued against petitioner-assessee by respondent-department under Section 83 - Respondent issued attachment orders on ground that petitioner had failed to discharge tax liability without any justification, further, respondent was of opinion that there was every chance that petitioner might default in paying ultimate tax, interest and penalty, for which a demand might be raised in assessment proceedings on completion - Petitioner filed instant writ petition seeking setting aside of bank account attachment order issued by respondent - Held:Supreme Court had opined that power to order a provisional attachment [under Section 83] of property of taxable person, including a bank account, was draconian in nature and conditions which were prescribed by statute for a valid exercise of power must be strictly followed - Further, apex court had further opined that exercise of power for ordering a provisional attachment must be preceded by formation of an opinion by Commissioner that “it is necessary so to do” for purpose of protecting interest of government revenue - Expression “necessary so to do for protecting government revenue” implicates that interests of government revenue could not be protected without ordering a provisional attachment - As aforesaid order applies with full force to facts of present case, therefore, attachments in FORM GST DRC-22 dated 05.04.2024 and order passed under Section 83 also dated 05.04.2024 were to be quashed [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Rule 159 of Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017] [Paras 3-6] [In favour of assessee]

Section 73 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962 - Demand and recovery - Assessee had a current account in IDFC Bank, Mumbai - Commissioner of Customs wrote letter dated 1-3-2019 to Branch Manager, IDFC Bank, Mumbai stating that department was conducting investigation in case of assessee and called upon him to provide certain details of bank account of assessee and also requested not to allow any withdrawal from said account and operation of locker without prior permission - On basis of above letter bank account of assessee had been frozen - Assessee filed writ petition seeking relief in this regard - In affidavit in reply filed by Customs Department it was stated that unfreezing frozen bank account would cause huge loss to Department - Whether an order in writing for provisional attachment of a bank account under section 110(5) of custom's Act is a must before such an account could be attached - Held, yes - Whether in absence of such an order in writing Competent Authority could not have provisionally attached bank account of assessee and continued with such attachment even beyond permissible extended period - Held, yes - Whether Competent Authority was to be directed to unfreeze bank account of assessee - Held, yes [Paras 33, 35 and 37] [In favour of assessee]GST/EXCISE/ST/VAT : An order in writing for provisional attachment of a bank account under section 110(5) of Custom’s Act is a must before such an account could be attached

GST/ST/VAT/EX : Where investigation under Central Goods and Services Tax Act was pending against assessee-company, impugned order of freezing bank account of assessee passed by Deputy Commissioner of Customs (Preventive) in view of investigation initiated against assessee by Anti-Evasion Wing of Central Goods and Services Tax, was unjustified and same was to be set aside

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Whether where specified proceedings had been launched against one taxable person, bank account of another taxable person could not have been provisionally attached, merely based on summons issued to him under section 70 - Held, yes - An inquiry was initiated against an export firm MG, as revenue suspected that MG was involved in fraudulent availing of Input Tax Credit, and this Input Tax Credit was utilised for payment of export goods, and later a refund was sought - Revenue scrutinised bank account of MG and noticed that a certain sum of money was transferred to one BE, on 19-6-2019 and 12-7-2019 - Revenue suspected these transactions were fictitious and no material was supplied to MG - Further, according to revenue BE transferred a certain sum of money to account of petitioner on 17-10-2019 - Petitioner was summoned under section 70 to give evidence and on same day, an order of provisional attachment of bank account of petitioner under section 83 was issued - Whether power to provisionally attach bank accounts is a drastic power and is not to be routinely exercised but, under section 83, legislature has conferred power on authorities to provisionally attach bank accounts to safeguard government revenue, and same is within well-defined ambit - Held, yes - Whether bank account of taxable person can be attached against whom proceedings under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74 as mentioned in section 83 are initiated - Held, yes - Whether therefore, in absence of proceedings initiated against petitioner under sections mentioned in section 83, order provisionally attaching bank account of petitioner, merely on basis of summons issued under section 70 was without jurisdiction and was liable to be quashed and set aside - Held, yes [Paras 14 to 17]GST : Where no proceedings were initiated/pending against petitioner under sections mentioned in section 83, order provisionally attaching bank account of petitioner merely on basis of summons issued under section 70 was without jurisdiction and was liable to be quashed and set aside

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Current account and Cash credit account - Communication in Form DRC-22 was addressed by Principal Commissioner to Bank Manager directing that proceedings had been lodged against petitioner under section 83 of CGST Act and, therefore, current account of petitioner was to be provisionally attached - Petitioner submitted that by virtue of attachment of account, apart from debit transfers all accounts were debit freezed - Not only current account, but in fact cash credit account was also provisionally attached - On writ, HELD : On more than one occasion, Court had deprecated practice of respondent authorities in seeking to enforce tax liabilities by provisionally attaching cash credit account - Notice was issued to respondent/s - Till returnable date, there would be ad-interim relief [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5, 6 and 7] [In favour of assessee]

Section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 83 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Demands and recovery - Provisional attachment - Petitioner, proprietor of a firm, received an attachment order evidencing that his bank account had been frozen at instance of GST authorities and despite his repeated requests, no information was disclosed by authority concerned as to why GST authority exercised such powers - However, it was found that no proceedings were pending against petitioner under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74 - Whether therefore, order provisionally attaching bank account of petitioner was without jurisdiction and was liable to be quashed and set aside; attachment was to be lifted and petitioner was to be permitted to operate his bank account - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 16]GST : Where no proceedings were pending against petitioner under sections 62, 63, 64, 67, 73 and 74, order provisionally attaching bank account of petitioner being without jurisdiction was to be lifted and petitioner was to be permitted to operate his bank account

Provisional attachment  -  Bank accounts- An order for provisional attachment under section 83 was passed against petitioner - Petitioner filed instant petition challenging same - Grievance of petitioner was that freezing of petitioner's bank accounts purportedly under section 83 as well as freezing of five bank accounts including cash credit accounts, was arbitrary and illegal - It was petitioner's contention that said action was ex facie without jurisdiction and in clear contravention of provisions of GST Act and Rules framed thereunder - HELD: Though petition has been heard from time to time and orders had been passed in respect of aforesaid petition, considering submissions as made by petitioner, submissions made on behalf of petitioner have considerable substance - Without delving into any other issue which may arise inter se between petitioner and respondents, in instant case by operation of law i.e. section 83(2), attachment has ceased to have effect - Therefore, petition was to be disposed declaring that impugned attachment had lapsed and further freezing of all 5 operational bank accounts of petitioner including Cash Credit Accounts had also stood lapsed - In any event it is settled law that Cash Credits cannot be provisionally attached - As a consequence thereof, petitioner would be free to operate its Bank accounts [Section  83  of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/  Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017][Para 4][In favour of assessee]

Demand of tax -  Assessee firm was involved in business of trading of containers for compressed or liquefied gas of iron and had discharged its tax liability without fail - Revenue authority informed assessee to furnish its return for supplies made or received and to discharge resultant tax liability for period under dispute, otherwise tax liability might be assessed-Revenue authority completed provisional assessment and assessee was issued with GST DRC-07 manually fastening liability under head taxes, interest and penalty-HELD: Impugned order had never been served upon assessee in manner prescribed under Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 Act - Due taxes had already been deposited way back in October 2020 itself- State Taxes department while intimating liability to assessee claimed only interest-Without any communication to assessee and soon thereafter cash credit and current account of assessee had been attached to recover entire amount in absence of any order passed by Commissioner which was beyond jurisdiction-Only interest amount could be recovered from assessee for delayed filing of returns but demand of entire amount was against principle of natural justice and was liable to be quashed [Sections 61 and 73 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/ Section Jharkhand Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 and 11] [In favour of assessee] Bank Account Attachment -  Assessee firm was involved in business of trading of containers for compressed or liquefied gas of iron and had discharged its tax liability without fail - Revenue authority informed assessee to furnish its return for supplies made or received and to discharge resultant tax liability for period under dispute, otherwise tax liability might be assessed- Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue had issued guidelines for provisional attachment of property and it was informed that every provisional attachment should cease to have effect after expiry of period of one year from date of provisional attachment-HELD: Power to attach bank account had to be only by way of order passed by Commissioner in order to protect interest of Government revenue and cash credit account not being as asset of assessee, same could not have been attached in any eventuality - Revenue authority failed to say and satisfy as to how authority of law had been followed and when assessee had never been extended any opportunity of hearing before passing of order complained of, nor have been communicated before attachment of bank account- Operation of order provisionally attaching bank account would cease to be operative after expiry of statutory period of one year- Letter of attachment/freezing bank account of assessee was quashed [Sections 61 and 73 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Jharkhand Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 12] [In favour of assessee]

Provisional attachment - Bank account - Where period of one year has expired after order defreezing assessee's bank account was passed, concerned bank would not interdict operations of petitioner's bank account on basis of impugned order [Section 83 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Delhi Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where period of one year has expired after order defreezing assessee's bank account was passed, concerned bank would not interdict operations of petitioner's bank account on basis of impugned order

facts.text:
The petitioner was the proprietor of the Firm running in the name and style of Global Corporation. He was involved in voluminous transactions of several parties and followed the law while conducting his business.

He received an attachment order and realized from the Office of the Principal Commissioner of Central GST, Mumbai that the Central Bank of India on 20-8-2020 freezed his current account with the Rajkot Main Branch and since then, he had not been allowed to operate the account.

The petitioner approached the Bank through its Manager and requested to let him be provided the necessary details for the reason of freezing his account. However, despite his repeated requests, no information was disclosed by the authority concerned as to why the GST authority exercised such powers. He was orally conveyed that because of voluminous transactions with the third party, which was involved in violation of the provisions of the CGST Act, his account has been frozen.

He moved an application under the Right to Information Act, 2005. The Reply received from the bank revealed that the information sought for could not be revealed on account of the fact that same would impede the process of investigation.

On Writ Petition before the High Court:

A search and seizure operation dated 28-4-2023 was conducted under section 132(1) and it was found that several persons/entities were involved in hawala transactions through bogus RTGS and cryptocurrencies. Pursuant to the said search and seizure operation and on the basis of certain suspicious transactions, the accounts of the assessees were debit frozen to avoid leakage of revenue.

The assessees by way of instant petition, sought directions to de-freeze the bank accounts and to set aside the letter dated 30-4-2023 issued by the respondents.

The assessee submitted that as per the mandate of section 132(8-A), the freezing of bank accounts ceases to have effect after the expiry of a period of sixty days. He, therefore, submitted that since the maximum period for which the bank accounts could have been frozen had already expired on 30-6-2023, there was no reason to proscribe the assessees to operate the bank accounts under consideration.

The Competent Authority provisionally attached under section 83 bank account of the assessee on the ground that it had created bogus records and claimed input tax credit for discharging the GST dues of about Rs. 121 crores.

The assessee, on writ petition filed before the High Court, contended that in terms of section 67 there could not be any attachment of future receivables so as to strangulate its entire business module and the recovery proceedings initiated by the department was contrary to the provisions of the GST Act.

The writ Court held that a sum of Rs. 5.68 crores, which was lying in the bank account of the assessee, was appropriated by the department and the assessee had also agreed to pay another sum of Rs. 1 crore against the estimated tax due of about Rs. 21 crores. The payment of Rs. 5.68 crores would amount to discharge of 27.05 per cent of the estimated tax dues. Therefore, there was no meaning in attaching the bank account further. It directed the assessee to deposit a sum of Rs. 1 crore within one week and on such deposit the attachment order was to be vacated. It also directed the Competent Authority to complete the investigation and issue appropriate show-cause notice as expeditiously as possible.

On writ appeal:

The assessee received a summons under section 70 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 from the authorities, directing the assessee to submit copy of GST payment along with other necessary details. The assessee appeared before the authority and submitted all necessary documents in response to the said summons. Thereafter another summons was issued which was replied by assessee. On the basis of reply furnished by assessee, the authority instructed the assessee to submit further documents, specific reasons and details as to why the input tax credit was wrongly claimed.

Subsequently, the proceedings were also initiated and a tax liability of certain amount was presumed by the authority since the assessee had claimed wrongful input tax credit and as such, with a view to safeguard the interest of revenue, by resorting to section 83 of the Act, the bank accounts were sought to be provisionally attached.

Instant writ petition was filed challenging the order of provisional attachment on the ground of violation of principles of natural justice. It was submitted by the assessee that to recover any amount of tax, interest and penalty, firstly, the assessment should be framed, and secondly, the demand notice should be issued and no conditions were fulfilled before attaching the bank account under section 83 of the CGST Act.

On the other hand, it was submitted by the department that the proceedings were already initiated under section 74 of Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 and to protect the interest of revenue, the bank account of assessee were attached by passing an order under section 83 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017. Further, the subjective satisfaction which had been arrived at by an authority could not be requested to be set at naught in extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court in the absence of any mala fide in the petition. Such discretion of an authority could not be usurped by the Court under article 226 of the Constitution of India.

The Competent Authority for recovery of GST dues had provisionally attached various bank accounts of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition seeking directions to the Competent Authority to release all bank accounts.

The petitioner filed appeals before the Commissioner (Appeals) along with applications for condonation of delay as also for stay on the assessment orders.

The petitioner, apprehending realization of amount pursuant to freezing of the bank accounts, filed the instant writ petition challenging coercive steps now taken by the respondents for realizing the amount determined by the assessment orders.

The petitioner sought to stay all further proceedings pursuant to freezing of bank accounts. The petitioner submitted that the substantial prayers and grounds were pending consideration in appeals. To prove bona fide of the petitioner, the petitioner offered to deposit 10 percent of the tax demanded in assessment orders for consideration and disposal of petitions for condonation of delay.

The respondent authority opposed the instant writ petitions and raised objection regarding maintainability of the instant writ prayers on the ground that the coercive steps were in the nature of execution of assessment orders which had become final. It was further submitted that the orders freezing bank accounts was either in continuation of tax liability already determined and the accounts were frozen only to recover the tax legitimately determined by the respondent. The respondents further contended that the appeals were filed with enormous delay and if petitioner was granted stay and allowed to operate bank accounts, the department would have to start the proceedings afresh, and in such an event, the department would suffer prejudice.

The petitioner was engaged in the business of manufacturing and supplying of various iron and steel products, viz., TMT bars, etc. and was paying goods and service tax in respect of the goods manufactured and supplied by it from the registered factory premises.

On 11-10-2018, the respondent- Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, visited the factory premises of the petitioner-company. During the course of such visit, he carried out comparison of the physical stocks of raw material and finished goods with the recorded quantity of the same and found that there was a stock difference, inasmuch as physical goods valued at Rs. 51,73,633 were found in excess in the factory premises when compared to the recorded quantity.

By an order of seizure dated 12-10-2018, the respondent attached the goods which according to him were found in excess on the factory premises of the petitioner.

It was the case of the petitioner that the respondent worked out the amount payable by the petitioner at Rs. 55,37,237 and thereafter on 22-10-2018, the bank accounts of the petitioner came to be attached by the first respondent.

It was the case of the petitioner that on account of seizure of its goods as well as attachment of the bank accounts, the petitioner was not in a position to carry on its day to day business and make payment of statutory dues like GST, Income tax, local taxes, etc.

The petitioner therefore, filed writ petition in High Court seeking defreezing of bank accounts and removal of attachment of goods.

The petitioner was engaged in the Business to Business ('B2B') e-commerce trading in 'white goods' including mobile handsets. The respondent No. 2 (Additional Director General of GST Intelligence) was conducting certain investigation in respect of Pal Overseas, a registered entity under the GST Act and also as regards other entities relating to the alleged issuance of bogus/fake invoices without supply of goods and were seeking to claim Input Tax Credit of Goods and Services Tax. It is stated that the petitioner was purchasing the mobile handsets from these suppliers and was selling to its customers. The respondent No. 2 conducted a search at the Head Office of the petitioner. During the search, the respondent No. 2 issued summons to the Associate Director of the petitioner Company and had recorded their statements.

The said representatives of petitioner Company responded to the notice, appeared before the Authorities and also made their statements, which had been duly recorded.

On 21-9-2020, the respondent No. 2 sought details of the bank accounts of the petitioner which were provided on the same day. It is stated that the respondent No. 2 attached the bank accounts of the petitioner purportedly in exercise of power under section 83.

The petitioner made representation in terms of rule 159(5) seeking release of attachment and defreezing of bank accounts, but such request was neither considered nor any order was passed as required under the applicable Rules.

On writ Petition:

■

The assessee, member of the Khasi Scheduled Tribe community, had filed his income tax returns claiming exemption under section 10(26).

■

An assessment order was then passed under sections 147, 144 and 144B treating certain business deposits as unexplained income under section 69A and consequently, a demand notice under section 156 was issued raising a tax demand

■

The assessee filed appeals before the Commissioner (Appeals) along with applications for condonation for delay, and also for stay of the demand under section 220(6).

■

In the meantime, however, the assessee’s bank accounts were frozen on instructions from the Income Tax Authorities and were set to be transferred to the Department.

■

On writ, the assessee approached the High Court seeking to invoke its powers under article 226 to de-freeze the bank accounts.

The Competent Authority had provisionally attached the bank accounts of the assessee under section 83 on the allegation that it without physical receipt of goods availed credit on basis of the invoices issued by the input supplier and thereafter paid GST on the basis of the output invoices without physical supply of the goods to the buyers.

Against the impugned order passed by the Competent Authority, the assessee filed a writ application.

It submitted that the allegation levied against it was to the effect that although the goods were not supplied, yet the tax was paid for the purpose of passing the credit. This was suggestive of the fact that, indisputably, no GST was payable, yet the same was paid. Section 9, which is the charging section, contemplates that the GST is payable only when the goods are supplied. The statement of output liability and input credit pertinent to it would indicate that for the period between July, 2017 and May, 2019, the total input credit availed of by it aggregated to Rs. 59.49 crores; whereas the total tax paid during the said period aggregated to Rs. 63.62 crores. The same was indicative of the fact that against the availment of credit of Rs. 59.49 crores, the tax amount to the tune of Rs. 63.62 crores came to be paid. Thus Rs. 4.13 crores had been paid in excess than the amount of credit availed of. If that be so, then there was no question of arriving at the satifaction by the Competent Authority that the interest of the government revenue was protected.

It further submitted that assuming for the moment that the allegation was true and correct and the credits were wrongly availed of, still the tax had been paid though it was not liable to be paid in light of the fact that there was no supply of goods. The availment of credits could be justified on two counts: (1) it was a revenue neutral satisfaction, and (2) the payment of tax although not payable yet was to be treated as if unavailable credits were reversed after they were wrongly availed.

■

The petitioner, a sole proprietor of a GST-registered firm engaged in sale and purchase of fisheries machineries, maintained a current account with the respondent bank. About Rs. 23 lakhs was credited to this account via RTGS from one Mrs. Anita allegedly towards purchase of machinery, and about Rs. 5 lakhs was withdrawn the same day. Shortly thereafter, when the petitioner attempted further withdrawal, bank officials orally informed that the account had been frozen. Despite repeated approaches, a text message to the Branch Manager, and a complaint/legal notice, the freeze continued, leading to this writ petition.

■

The respondent bank stated that it froze the account due to suspicious transactions, citing that the petitioner had declared annual income of about Rs. 5.76 lakhs at the time of opening the current account while a large sum of about Rs. 23 lakhs was credited and Rs. 5 lakhs was withdrawn the same day. It relied on Section 12(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 to justify the freeze as a precaution to restrict further debits, issued a letter seeking transaction details, and on its inquiry stated that the Rs. 23 lakhs was credited by Bank of Maharashtra under a loan to Smt. Anita and that Bank of Maharashtra requested by email that the amount not be released and be refunded.

■

Before the High Court on writ petition.

The assessee-company was carrying on the business in the real estate and the petitioner No. 2 who was the managing director of said company was doing the business in Kirana goods. Pursuant to a search conducted at the residential premises of the managing director of the company, the officials of the Excise Department seized certain documents, computer and cash. The company was having a current account with the bank and also had four FDRs. Subsequently, the officials of the Excise Department freezed the said bank account of the assessee. Thereafter, the assessee filed the writ petition whereby the assessee was held to be entitled to operate the said bank accounts. The Excise Department in pursuance of the direction given by the Court informed the bank to release the freezed account. On the same day, the ITO passed the order exercising the powers conferred on him under section 281B. The said order was passed in order to protect the interest of the revenue as in the opinion of the Assessing Officer, a substantial demand was likely to arise against the assessee as a result of the assessment proceedings under section 153A consequent to the search and seizure under section 132A. The order was passed with the approval of the Commissioner.

In writ assessee’s case was that the exercise of power under section 281B was wholly unwarranted, illegal and arbitrary and in impugned order had been passed without their being any material in possession of the department to form an opinion that there was likelihood of a substantial demand against the assessee.

The petitioner-assessee was registered society under Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002. The business of the society was to run the scheme for its members and to facilitate the investment. It filed revised return wherein returned loss was enhanced.

During assessment, the Assessing Officer made certain queries related with creditworthiness, genuineness and identity of the investors of society but assessee was not co-operating in furnishing the requisite information. Malpractice was said to have been adopted by the petitioner. In regular assessment, it was found that total income of the petitioner was to be assessed at Rs. 1100 crores and tentative tax liability was of Rs. 445 crores.

In order to protect the interests of revenue, the Assessing Officer provisionally attached the bank accounts of the assessee after proposed action was approved in writing by the Commissioner.

On writ, the assessee submitted that:

-

By means of attachment of all the accounts of the petitioner, the business had come to standstill.

-

Reasonable opportunity of being heard, should have been provided to the assessee to whom the order was proposed.

■

The corporate debtor was undergoing CIRP and moratorium under section 14 was in force. During subsistence of moratorium, Respondent No.1 issued a notice in Form GST DRC-13 to the banker of the corporate debtor (Respondent No.2) claiming about ₹4.33 crores towards alleged pending GST dues. Respondent No.2 furnished details of four current accounts of the corporate debtor, only one of which reflected an available balance of about ₹83.89 lakhs, and placed the accounts under 'No Debit' status pursuant to the notice.

■

Respondent No.1 thereafter generated a challan for ₹83.89 lakhs, pursuant to which Respondent No.2 remitted the said amount on 12-7-2022 from the corporate debtor’s account. The remittance was made without authorization of the erstwhile Resolution Professional or authorised signatory and during subsistence of the moratorium. The erstwhile RP had, by letter dated 8-10-2020, informed Respondent No.2 of his appointment and specifically directed that no withdrawals be permitted without his authorization.

■

Subsequently, the erstwhile RP intimated Respondent No.1 about commencement of CIRP and moratorium, to which an officer of Respondent No.1 replied on 28-7-2022 seeking guidance on filing of claim. This correspondence occurred after the amount of ₹83.89 lakhs had already been withdrawn. Respondent No.1 thereafter filed its claim, which was rejected by the erstwhile RP as being filed beyond the prescribed time.

■

Upon assuming office, the applicant/RP sought complete details of the remittance from Respondent No.2 and also placed on record confirmation from the suspended director that no authorization had been given to the bank for such withdrawal. The applicant thereafter repeatedly sought refund of the amount recovered in violation of the moratorium; however, despite assurances, no response was received from the concerned officer.

■The

applicant/RP therefore filed the present application under section 60(5) seeking refund of ₹83.89 lakhs remitted to Respondent No.1 during moratorium and without authorization. The applicant further contended that Respondent No.1 had frozen various bank accounts of the corporate debtor maintained with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank, in contravention of section 14, and sought directions for immediate de-freezing of the said accounts, as such action impeded discharge of duties under section 25 of the Code.

■

The assessee filed its return of income declaring income/loss of Rs. 10.69 lakhs.

■

The Assessing Officer passed an assessment order determining the income at Rs. 41.22 crores.

■

The assessee filed an appeal against the assessment order and also filed an application praying for stay of the demand issued under section 156.

■

The Deputy Commissioner rejected the application for stay of demand and directed the assessee to deposit 20 per cent of the disputed demand.

■

Thereafter, the Principal Commissioner also rejected the application for stay of the entirety of the disputed demand and directed the assessee to make a payment of at least 20 per cent of the demand immediately.

■

Meanwhile, the Deputy Commissioner passed an order attaching the assessee''s bank account.

■

In instant writ, the assessee challenged the order of attachment and sought for a direction to de-freeze the bank account.

The Assistant Commissioner directed the assessee's bankers to freeze the assessee's accounts with them.

On writ:

A search operation was conducted at the premises of the assessee-company, a wholly owned subsidiary of FCS, Taiwan. During search, several materials, digital data, books of account and documents were seized.

The Assessing Officer was of believe that the assessee was involved in various methods of tax evasion like unaccounted cash sales, purchase through shell companies etc. and thus attached the assessee's HSBC and DBS bank accounts after seeking approval from the Principal Commissioner under section 281B.

Later on, the DBS bank account was directed to be converted into fixed deposits and subsequently, the bank account of DBS Bank was released, whereas, the balance funds remained under attachment until further orders.

The assessee in instant writ petition challenged the continuing of the attachment of HSBC bank account and DBS bank accont even after a period of six months from date of order passed under section 132(9C) and contended that it had seriously jeopardized its business operation.

Bank accounts of assessee were provisionally attached to protect revenue's interest under section 231B

Subsequently, regular assessment was framed and total tax demand was raised against assessee.

The assessee filed instant writ petition claiming that amount attached standing to his credit over and above the demand raised against him should have been released by revenue on completion of assessment.

The assessee-company had certain credits in the form of input tax credit as on 30-6-2017.

Under the GST Act there is a provision to pay tax either by cash or by way of credits which were available to the credit of a dealer as on 30-6-2017.

The Competent Authority called upon the assessee to pay interest amounting to Rs. 1.64 crores towards delay in payment of GST for seven months from July, 2017 to Jaunary, 2018 and thereafter issued a communication dated 3-5-2019 for attachment of bank account of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition praying to quash the impugned communication dated 3-5-2019 as illegal, arbitrary and violative of principle of natural justice. It stated that when it became liable to pay GST from July, 2017, it choose to pay the tax by way of input tax credit which stood to its credit as on 30-6-2017, but could not pay GST solely owing to technical glitch in department's portal.

The applicant was a proprietor of a proprietary concern engaged in the business of trading of ferrous and non-ferrous metal scrap. It held a valid registration certificate under the provisions of the CGST Act and the GGST Act respectively.

A spot visit was carried out by the flying squad of the revenue department at the premises of the applicant. The department was prima facie of the view that the purchases made by the applicant from the JSK and UM were not genuine. In the course of the search carried out by the department, the registers, documents and books of account for the period between 1-7-2017 and 11-8-2020 were collected and taken into possession.

The Additional Commissioner passed an order under section 83 of provisional attachment of cash credit/current bank account and one savings bank account held by the applicant with the HDFC Bank Ltd.

Being dissatisfied with the order of provisional attachment, the applicant filed the instant writ-application.

The assessee-company was engaged in supply of wheat flour, meslin flour, cereal flour etc. which would invite SGST and CGST at prescribed rates.

On 20-2-2018, the departmental authorities visited the petitioners' (assessee's) work premises and noticed that the petitioners were not paying any tax either on branded or unbranded goods. According to the petitioners, under threat and coercion, the departmental authorities collected three cheques even before the petitioners' tax liability was ascertained.

On 27-2-2018, the department issued a show-cause notice calling upon the petitioners why CGST and SGST totalling to Rs. 36,88,706 not be recovered for the period between July 2017 and 20-2-2018; and simultaneously, on the same date, the department wrote to the petitioners' banks provisionally attaching the petitioners' said bank accounts and instructed the banks not to allow the petitioners to operate the accounts without the prior permission of the department.

On 19-3-2018, the adjudicating authority issued fresh notice under the purported exercise of powers under section 74(3) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act calling upon the petitioners to show cause why a sum of Rs. 1,29,13,928 towards CGST and SGST not be recovered from the period between july 2017 and 20-2-2018. This second show-cause notice, the petitioners had challenged on the ground of lack of jurisdiction.

The petitioners challenged the three actions of the departmental authorities in the instant petition.

■

The assessee filed its return declaring income.

■

The return was selected for scrutiny and a high-pitched assessment order was passed assessing the income of assessee.

■

The assessee filed an appeal against the assessment order. However, the appeal was pending disposal before the Commissioner (Appeals).

■

Meanwhile, the Assessing Officer had recovered certain amount by adjusting the refund due to the assessee for the subsequent years.

■

In instant writ, the assessee prayed for stay of demand and was aggrieved by the action of the revenue in freezing its bank account.

The Competent Authority for recovery of Rs. 3 crore from the assessee had provisionally attached its six bank accounts.

The assessee filed a writ petition stating that it had a large amount of cash lying at its disposal with the concerned banks.

The Assessing Authority conducted a search at the business premises of the assessee, a proprietorship concern, and on the basis of the material found calculated the cumulative liability of the old concerns of assessee under the VAT Act on presumptive basis at Rs. 4.50 crores.

Thereupon the assessee offered its immovable property of Rs. 5 crores as security in order to avoid dispute till completion of the assessment proceedings.

However, the Commissioner by an order passed under section 45 provisionally attached the above immovable property of the assessee. He also provisionally attached the bank accounts of the assessee. He further issued garnishee notice under section 44 directing the bank of the assessee to make payment from the bank account of the assessee.

The assessee filed a writ petition praying the High Court to quash and set aside the impugned order of provisional attachment of the bank accounts and garnishee notice.

The assessee filed instant writ petition challenging the order passed under section 83 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 whereby the various bank accounts of the assessee were provisionally attached. However, no further orders were passed for recovering any dues. It was submitted by the department that the inquiries had revealed that the assessee was a non-existing person and had not cooperated in the investigation and hence order of provisional attachment was justified.

The Competent Authority of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Department had provisionally attached the bank accounts of the petitioner under section 83.

On writ:

■

Petitioners had issued cheques to respondent towards a payment. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of the CGST issued a communication to the bank and petitioner’s bank account was provisionally attached by the CGST Department under section 83 of the CGST Act, 2017, thereby prohibiting any debit transactions.

■

This order effectively froze the account and restricted all transactions. The same was confirmed by the bank’s letter, stating that a “STOP” had been marked on the account pursuant to the CGST attachment order and that no transactions could be permitted until further instructions were received from the department.

■

The petitioners duly informed the respondent of this attachment and requested that the cheques be not presented until the account was de-freezed.

■

Despite this, the respondent presented the cheques for encashment, leading to their dishonour and filed complaint under section 138 against the petitioners.

■

The petitioners filed petition seeking quashing of the summons and the consequential proceedings arising out of complaint case on ground that they informed the respondent about the attachment of their bank account by the CGST Department under section 83 of the CGST Act, 2017, as soon as it occurred. They contend that the cheques were issued with a mutual understanding that they would not be presented without prior intimation and consent. Despite this, the respondent presented the cheques for encashment, leading to their dishonour.

The assessee was a dealer in electrical components. On 2-8-2012 the Commercial Tax Officer (Enforcement) inspected the assessee's business premises in terms of section 65 and noticed various defects and discrepancies in its account books. Thereupon he forcibly collected a cheque for an amount of Rs. 3.75 lakhs from the assessee towards tax due on the alleged defects.

The assessee made a representation before the Assessing Authority concerned, wherein all the defects noticed had been explained and he had been requested to withhold the cheque amount of Rs. 3.75 lakhs which was forcibly collected by the Commercial Tax Officer (Enforcement) at the time of inspection.

Thereafter the Assessing Authority having found that the department's bank had returned the above cheque unrealised issued a notice to the bank of assessee attaching its bank account for the recovery of the amount of Rs. 3.75 lakhs.

On writ:

The petitioner company carried on its business transactions through the current account registered with bank. On 5-6- 2018, the Additional Director General, Directorate General of Goods & Services Tax Intelligence (ADGGI) passed an Order to provisionally attach the current account of the petitioner maintained in the said bank under Section 83 of the CGST Act, 2017. The said first Order of the ADGGI was addressed to the Branch Manager of the said bank in order to freeze the functioning of the said account of the petitioners.

The said bank through a letter dated 11-6- 2018, informed the writ petitioner about the Order passed by the ADGGI which directed the bank to freeze the current account of the petitioners.

On 19-7- 2019, the said company by way of a letter made representation before the ADGGI, requesting to de-freeze the current account of the company which was earlier provisionally attached under Section 83. On 31-7-2019, the petitioner company wrote to the said bank praying for immediate de-freezing of the said account.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the inaction on the part of the respondents the writ petitioner preferred a writ application before the Court. . Thereafter, on 31-10- 2019, the Principal Additional Director General, Directorate General of Goods & Services Tax Intelligence (PDDGI) passed a fresh provisional order directing the said bank to provisionally attach the said current account of the petitioner.

The writ petitioners filed instant writ petition aggrieved by the orders passed by the Directorate General of Goods and Services Tax Intelligence [DGGI], to provisionally attach the current bank accounts of the writ petitioner under Section 83.

On assessee's appeal, Tribunal ordered 15 per cent pre-deposit and stayed balance demand for a period of 6 months.

On expiry of 6 months, department directed assessee to make balance pre-deposit.

Assessee filed an application before Tribunal seeking extension of stay and informed department of that fact but, in meantime, department freezed assessee's bank account under Section 87 on 21-1-2014 and recovered some amount.

Tribunal granted extension of stay vide order dated 23-1-2014 on ground that delay in disposing of appeal was not attributable to assessee.

On receipt of Tribunal's order, Department defreezed bank account with effect from 28-1-2014.
